Pohyb ruské sabotážní skupiny Černí Rusové byl důvodem rozsáhlé operace polských bezpečnostních sil u hranic s ruskou Kaliningradskou oblastí. Uvedl to polský veřejnoprávní rozhlas Polskie Radio 24. Varšava na severovýchodě svého území zřídila speciální jednotku. Reagovala tak na varování rozvědky před možnými ruskými sabotážemi a vpády přes hranice.
Foto: Kuba Stezycki, Reuters
Polští vojáci z 18. mechanizované divize hlídají polskou hranici s Běloruskem
Článek
„V reakci na hrozbu sabotáží posílily polské bezpečnostní složky ochranu hranic,“ vysvětlila stanice přesuny na polské straně hranice s ruskou Kaliningradskou oblastí. Velení polských bezpečnostních sil vyslalo do Podlaského a Varmijsko-mazurského vojvodství posily, včetně příslušníků polské speciální jednotky GROM, dalších příslušníků pohraniční stráže a policejních protiteroristických jednotek.
Podle polského premiéra Donalda Tuska se posily aktivovaly, když pohraničníci v noci na úterý zaznamenali…

titulekPuvodni: Norway strengthens border surveillance system to detect drones near Russia
shrnuti: Norway is deploying NASAMS sensors in Kirkenes and reinforcing its military presence with over 30 soldiers to detect drones near the Russian border.

vyrez.text:
Norway deploys drone detection system near Russian border | Ukrainska Pravda
The Norwegian flag. Photo: Getty Images
The Norwegian Armed Forces are deploying an aerial surveillance system in the town of Kirkenes, near the Russian border, to detect drones that stray off course at an early stage.
Source: a press release by the Norwegian government, as reported by European Pravda
Details: The Norwegian Air Force is deploying specialised NASAMS sensors, while the military garrison in the region will be reinforced by more than 30 soldiers.
Advertisement:





"We have seen in other countries that drones can go astray. This is something Norway takes seriously. We must be prepared, even though we do not currently see an increased aerial threat to Norway or the population of Finnmark," said Norwegian Defence Minister Tore O. Sandvik.
The government noted that the measures are preventive and are not linked to any specific new threat.
The sensors are designed to detect drones, warn of their presence and provide a comprehensive picture of all activity in the airspace over border areas.

shrnuti: Latvia issued an air-raid warning in two eastern municipalities overnight after an unidentified drone entered its airspace and crashed near the Russian border.

Aircraft. Stock photo: MIL.LV/LV
An air-raid warning was issued in Latvia's Ludza and Balvi municipalities on the night of 2-3 November after an unidentified drone was detected. The object crashed in the Balvi area.
Source: European Pravda, citing the Latvian National Armed Forces
Details: An air-raid warning was issued in the Ludza and Balvi municipalities at 00:10 on 2 November. Fighter jets from NATO's Baltic Air Defence mission were deployed in the airspace over the Baltic states. In response to the threat, the Latvian Armed Forces also deployed interceptor drones.

According to early reports, the object that triggered the alert crashed in the Balvi municipality, near the Russian border. Ground search operations have begun there.
The Latvian National Armed Forces urged members of the public not to approach or touch any suspicious objects or debris they might find and to call the emergency number 112 immediately.

shrnuti: Latvia has activated an orange alert in eastern districts and deploys a Blaze interceptor drone after an unidentified UAV breaches its airspace.

vyrez.text:

Latvia on map. Photo: google.maps
The Latvian Armed Forces have deployed a drone interceptor after an unidentified unmanned aerial vehicle breached Latvian airspace on the evening of 1 November.
Source: European Pravda , citing Latvian media outlet LSM
Details: An
orange alert
An orange alert in Latvia refers to a high-level warning issued by authorities either for airspace threats (such as detected drones or aircraft) or for severe weather conditions (such as violent thunderstorms and heavy hail)
was declared in the Krāslava and Ludza districts of Latvia after an unidentified drone violated the nation's airspace at 18:59 on Sunday.
Advertisement:





Seventeen minutes later, the flying object exited Latvian airspace, crossing back over the Latvian-Russian border.
The Latvian military reacted to the detected threat to its airspace by launching a Blaze interceptor drone. At 19:19, the decision was taken to activate the interceptor's self-destruct mechanism to prevent any potential risk of violating the state border with Russia.

shrnuti: Romania sent four F-16s and a helicopter after two drones entered its airspace on 31 October, triggering alerts in six counties; no crashes reported.

vyrez.text:
Romania scrambles four F-16s after two drones violate its airspace | Ukrainska Pravda
A fighter jet. Stock photo: Getty Images
Radar surveillance systems operated by Romania's Ministry of National Defence detected two unmanned aerial vehicles that had entered the country's airspace without authorisation on the evening of 31 October.
Source: Romania's Ministry of National Defence , as reported by European Pravda
Details: Romania scrambled four F-16 fighter jets and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter to monitor the situation and manage the response after two unmanned aerial vehicles violated the country's airspace.
Advertisement:





Alerts were issued in six Romanian counties due to the airspace violation: Iași, Neamț, Vaslui, Botoșani, Bacău and Suceava.
One of the two drones left the country's airspace, while the other was last spotted in the area between the counties of Vaslui and Bacău.
No drone crashes were reported.
Background:
On the same day, a drone violated Moldovan airspace during Russian aerial attacks on Ukraine.

Ukraine’s armed forces is carrying out a massive, hours-long drone attack on Omsk.
Omsk Governor Vitaliy Khotsenko declared a drone threat alert on November 11 at 12:40 p.m. Moscow time. It remained in effect as of 8:10 p.m. Moscow time. Six hours into the attack, Khotsenko urged residents to stay indoors.
Amid the attack, authorities in Omsk have canceled entertainment and sports events planned for November 11: theater and ballet performances, the Sila Sibiri “Power of Siberia” figure skating Grand Prix, as well as the opening of the Dostoevsky.Omsk theater festival.
The targets and aftermath of the attack remain unconfirmed. Citing eyewitnesses, local Telegram channels reported that a fire broke out at the Omsk oil refinery and that a power plant may also have been damaged.
It is the second time since the war in Ukraine began that authorities have also declared a drone threat…

Bombendrohungen an 6.000 Schulen in Italien
Stand: 11.11.2026 • 16:31 Uhr
An Tausenden Schulen in Italien sind per E-Mail Bombendrohungen eingegangen. Auch in Großbritannien gibt es ähnliche Fälle. Die Behörden gehen von Falschmeldungen aus. Wer hinter den Drohungen steckt, ist unklar.
Etwa 6.000 Schulen in Italien haben E-Mails mit Bombendrohungen erhalten. Die Regierung gab inzwischen Entwarnung: Italiens Ministerpräsidentin Giorgia Meloni betonte, nach den bisher durchgeführten Überprüfungen gebe es keinerlei Hinweise auf eine konkrete Gefahr. Vorsorglich waren nach Regierungsangaben dennoch mindestens 300 Schulen evakuiert worden.
Von den Behörden gab es zunächst keine Angaben zu möglichen Hintergründen der Bombendrohungen. Meloni schrieb auf Facebook von einer "Strategie, die darauf abzielt, Beunruhigung und Sorge zu schüren". Sie kündigte eine umfassende Untersuchung der Vorfälle an und berief eine Krisensitzung der Regierung ein.

Authorities are investigating the origin of the messages, although police have not confirmed the email address from which they were sent.

11.11.2026 12.50

Eine anonyme Bombendrohung hat heute an rund 300 Schulen in Italien Alarm ausgelöst. Betroffen waren Bildungseinrichtungen in mehreren Städten. Schüler und Schulpersonal wurden vorsorglich evakuiert. Polizeikräfte durchsuchten die Gebäude nach möglichen Sprengsätzen.
Besonders viele Schulen waren in Rom betroffen. Die Schulleitungen verständigten die Polizei, die zur Räumung der Gebäude riet. Der Absender der Droh-E-Mails gab sich Medienberichten zufolge als Vertreter einer terroristischen Organisation aus.
Krisensitzung einberufen
Die italienische Regierung reagierte mit einer kurzfristig einberufenen Krisensitzung unter der Leitung von Ministerpräsidentin Giorgia Meloni. Der italienische Verteidigungsminister Guido Crosetto verurteilte die Bombendrohungen. Sie seien Teil einer „Strategie, Angst und Besorgnis zu verbreiten“.
Die Sicherheitskräfte seien gerade damit beschäftigt, ernst zu nehmende Drohungen von den Taten profilierungssüchtiger Menschen zu unterscheiden, sagte der Minister. Solche Fälle würden leider…

On Poland’s Independence Day, FSB says it detained two Poles in Russia on espionage charges
November 11, 2026, 9:22 am
Source: Meduza
Russia’s FSB arrested two Polish citizens in the Kaliningrad region on espionage charges, its Public Relations Center said.
A Polish intelligence “network of agents” had been operating in the region, the FSB said.
It said they collected and passed on information about Russian military personnel and Defense Ministry facilities, as well as “information about the socio-economic situation, and migration and social policy” in the region.
The FSB also issued official warnings against espionage and treason to seven more Polish citizens and three Russian citizens who had contact with Polish intelligence services. The seven Poles were barred from entering Russia “for an extended period.”
The FSB made the announcement on Poland’s Independence Day, which falls on November 11.

He said the attack targeted the port zone of Ust-Luga, in the Kingisepp district. Several drones hit the area, sparking a fire and injuring three port workers. A transformer substation in Ust-Luga also experienced an emergency shutdown.
The drone attack forced the closure of Pulkovo Airport. Passenger planes flying to St. Petersburg from Istanbul and Hurghada landed in Helsinki instead. By morning, 30 outbound flights from Pulkovo were delayed .
Smolensk region also came under drone attack, and air defenses shot down 37 drones, said the region’s governor, Vasily Anokhin. In the city of Yartsevo, “debris” hit a multi-story building, sparking a fire. Two people died.

Garry Kasparov, a Russian opposition figure and the 13th world chess champion, canceled a trip to Berlin after security services warned of a possible threat to his life, the German tabloid Bild reported.
Kasparov was scheduled to speak at Berlin Freedom Week. Instead, he recorded a video address for participants, in which he acknowledged reports that Russia was trying to kill him. He said security professionals had strongly advised him against traveling to Berlin because the trip would be an unjustifiable risk under the circumstances.
Kasparov also criticized European authorities for not doing enough to counter the Russian government, accusing European politicians of letting Europe become a playground for Vladimir Putin. If Putin could reach him there, Kasparov warned, he could reach anyone.

titulekPuvodni: Poland arrests two Ukrainians suspected of spying and sabotage for Russia
shrnuti: Two Ukrainian citizens, ages 24 and 25, have been arrested in Poland on suspicion of espionage and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence services, said Tomasz Siemoniak, the Polish minister who coordinates the country’s intelligence services.

vyrez.text:
Poland arrests two Ukrainians suspected of spying and sabotage for Russia — Meduza
Skip to main content
Poland arrests two Ukrainians suspected of spying and sabotage for Russia
November 10, 2026, 5:09 pm
Source: Internal Security Agency of Poland (ABW)
Two Ukrainian citizens, ages 24 and 25, have been arrested in Poland on suspicion of espionage and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence services, said Tomasz Siemoniak, the Polish minister who coordinates the country’s intelligence services.
Investigators allege that the two photographed critical infrastructure and military facilities in Poland and set cars on fire. They replaced vehicle license plates with plates from Ukrainian military vehicles to deflect suspicion. They were paid for these tasks, including in cryptocurrency.
Poland’s Internal Security Agency said both suspects have been ordered held in custody for three months. They face sentences ranging from 10 years to life in prison, the agency said.

By Hugh Schofield in Paris
Published

One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters.
After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir.
With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces.
President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans.
"She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media.

Der polnische Inlandsgeheimdienst ABW hat zwei ukrainische Staatsbürger festgenommen. Das bestätigte der für die Geheimdienstkoordination zuständige Innenminister Tomasz Siemoniak heute der Nachrichtenagentur PAP.
Die beiden Männer stünden im Verdacht, im Auftrag russischer Geheimdienste Spionage betrieben und Sabotageakte verübt zu haben.
Die beiden Männer hätten in Polen kritische Infrastruktureinrichtungen sowie militärische Anlagen fotografiert, hatte zuvor schon die Agentur für Innere Sicherheit (ABW) auf der Plattform X mitgeteilt. Dafür sollen sie unter anderem mit Kryptowährungen bezahlt worden sein.
Kennzeichen ersetzt, Fahrzeuge angezündet
Die ABW vermutet in ihrer Mitteilung, die Festgenommenen hätten versucht, den Verdacht auf die Ukraine zu lenken: „Den Ermittlungen zufolge setzten sie Fahrzeuge in Brand, wobei sie zuvor deren Kennzeichen durch solche ersetzten, die denen der ukrainischen Armee ähnelten.“

Armenian investigators told RFE/RL that they launched a criminal probe into the assault allegations and had ordered a forensic medical examination after the Ukrainian man, identified as Dmytro Samuelenko, filed a police report.

Swathes of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators, in some cases forcing them to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.
"I can confirm that this attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of the Islamic Republic of Iran," Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said of the cyberattacks.

Skip to main content
Advertisement
PARIS — French Minister of Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran was behind the recent series of “unprecedented” cyberattacks on refrigerators in several major supermarket chains in the country last month.
“Thanks to the outstanding work of the government departments, I am able to confirm that responsibility for this attack lies with the Iranian Revolutionary Guards,” Barrot told reporters Monday at a G7 meeting in Paris. “We will impose sanctions at European level against those responsible.”
Barrot said that 700 food distribution sites in France were impacted in the cyberattack. French prosecutors said shortly after that they were opening an investigation into the hacks.
Though Barrot was only referring to the incidents reported in France, grocery stores across Europe and even French blood banks have been targeted by hackers in recent days. The life Vasilij Kovacs knew ended with a bang. It was late afternoon on March 1, 2025, when an armored vehicle smashed through the metal gate of the old farmhouse where he lived southeast of the Latvian capital, Riga.
Masked men emerged with their guns drawn. They belonged to Latvia’s State Security Service, the country’s counterintelligence agency. The officers searched the property, seizing several mobile phones, SIM cards and documents, along with a pistol with its serial number filed off, a bayonet from an AK-47 and a cellphone jammer, according to a search report later filed by the authorities. They arrested Kovacs, a Ukrainian man in his 60s who has lived in Latvia for more than 30 years.
In March, Kovacs was transferred to stand trial in Lithuania, where he is accused of planning terrorist attacks, alongside four alleged accomplices. Five others face trial in Warsaw.
